pin_corrections_needed.issue: The published pin for hkg_005 (The King Camphor of Sha Lo Wan) sits roughly 303 metres from the government register's own coordinate for the same tree. Published: 22.285321, 113.900627. Register (AFCD/KS/005, tr_no AFCD/IS/00001, 'Sha Lo Wan Tsuen, Lantau (The slope next to the school)', in data/registers/hongkong-ovt.json, dbh 2200mm, height 19m): 22.283796, 113.903071. Both describe the identical tree by name and location text ('the slope next to Sha Lo Wan School'), so this is a coordinate discrepancy on the same tree, not two different trees. hkg_005's own notes in hong-kong.json say its coordinates were 'converted from its HK1980 Grid reference (808051/816127)' using a manual Transverse Mercator inverse transform implemented and self-checked in an earlier session (see hkg_001's notes for the method). The data/registers/hongkong-ovt.json entries carry latitude/longitude directly, no grid conversion needed, which is very likely a direct WGS84 field the AFCD register itself provides. CONCLUSION: the register's direct lat/lon (22.283796, 113.903071) is more likely correct than the earlier session's manually converted point, because it skips a conversion step that is a known source of error (the HK1980 Grid to WGS84 transform is exactly the kind of arithmetic that is easy to get subtly wrong, and this project's own notes on hkg_001 describe that transform as self-implemented and self-checked rather than independently verified). This pass did NOT edit hong-kong.json (verification passes do not edit city files); recorded here for a pin-correction pass to action. Recommend re-deriving hkg_001 through hkg_004 and hkg_006's coordinates the same way, from data/registers/hongkong-ovt.json's direct lat/lon fields where a matching ovt_no exists, and comparing each against the currently published pin before trusting the manual grid conversion for any of them.

leads.reason: dbh 2710mm, height 20m, crown spread 34m, the largest candidate in the Central district, 3143m from hkg_001 and roughly 3km from the Forbes Street/Ka Wai Man Road cluster. The brief specifically asked whether any stonewall or notable trees sit 'within reach of the existing Kowloon Park cluster or Central'; this is the strongest Central candidate found, but at 3+ km from every currently published tree it would need to anchor a wholly new 'Central' cluster rather than extend an existing walk, which this topping-up pass (needing only 4 trees) did not have room for. Strong candidate for a future Hong Kong deepening pass built around Hong Kong Park / Central specifically.
